title: Broadcast the Backscatter — Our View FROM the Sky. Not a Prediction.

the_principle.statement: the thymus broadcasts what we SEE, not what we PREDICT. it's a weather radar, not a fortune teller. the forecast is observation at distance — seeing the storm that already exists but hasn't reached us yet.
the_principle.klein: everything visible inside the Klein surface IS visible in the RSS feed. the backscatter we see AND the forecast of what we see coming. our view FROM the sky.

the_original_weather_science.note: the entire history of weather forecasting is the history of OBSERVATION, not prediction. every breakthrough was seeing further, not guessing better.

bjerknes_1904.what: published the first paper proposing weather could be forecast by solving nonlinear partial differential equations
bjerknes_1904.insight: weather is not magic. it is PHYSICS. if you know the current state and the equations, the future state is determined.
bjerknes_1904.our_analog: the thymus selection table IS the equations. the Caddy access log IS the current state. the immune forecast IS the future state — not predicted, COMPUTED.
bjerknes_1904.ref: Bjerknes, V. (1904). 'Das Problem der Wettervorhersage, betrachtet vom Standpunkte der Mechanik und der Physik.' Meteorologische Zeitschrift, 21, 1-7.

bergen_school_1917.who: Vilhelm Bjerknes + son Jacob Bjerknes + Halvor Solberg + Tor Bergeron
bergen_school_1917.what: founded the Bergen School of Meteorology. invented the concept of FRONTS — boundaries between warm and cold air masses. named after WWI battlefronts.

key_concepts.fronts: sloping boundaries between different air masses. warm front = warm air riding OVER cold. cold front = cold air pushing UNDER warm.
key_concepts.polar_front_theory: weather activity concentrates in narrow zones between polar cold air and tropical warm air. cyclones form as waves on this front.
key_concepts.cyclone_lifecycle: birth → growth → occlusion → decay. the cyclone has a LIFECYCLE just like a cell.
key_concepts.air_mass_analysis: classify the atmosphere by its ORIGIN — tropical maritime, polar continental, etc. the air mass IS its identity.

our_analog.fronts: the boundary between self and non-self traffic. warm front = organic visitors rising over baseline. cold front = attack wave pushing under normal traffic.
our_analog.polar_front: the thymus selection table IS the polar front. self-traffic (warm) meets non-self (cold) at the classification boundary.
our_analog.cyclone_lifecycle: attack patterns have lifecycles: birth (first probe) → growth (escalation) → occlusion (peak) → decay (antibody response). EXACTLY like weather.
our_analog.air_mass_analysis: classify requests by ORIGIN — human browser, search engine, AI scraper, attack tool. the user-agent IS the air mass identity.

bergen_school_1917.ref: Bjerknes, J. and Solberg, H. (1922). 'Life cycle of cyclones and the polar front theory.' Geophysical Publications, 3(1).

richardson_1922.who: Lewis Fry Richardson (1881-1953), British mathematician and pacifist
richardson_1922.what: published 'Weather Prediction by Numerical Process' — the first attempt to forecast weather using mathematical computation

the_story.battlefield: Richardson was a Quaker ambulance driver in WWI France. between transporting wounded soldiers, he computed the weather by hand on a heap of hay in a cold rest billet.
the_story.first_forecast: 6 weeks of calculation for a single 6-hour forecast at one point. used a slide rule and log tables. the result was wildly wrong (145 hPa pressure change vs actual ~1 hPa).
the_story.why_wrong: not the method — the INITIAL DATA was unbalanced. the method is exactly how modern weather prediction works. Richardson was right about everything except the data quality.
the_story.lost_manuscript: his draft was lost in the war, then found months later under a heap of coal. the book nearly didn't exist.

the_forecast_factory.what: Richardson's vision of a 'forecast factory' — a huge circular theater with a map of the world painted on walls and ceiling
the_forecast_factory.workers: 64,000 human 'computers', each responsible for one grid cell of the atmosphere
the_forecast_factory.coordination: a conductor in the center using colored signal lights to keep computation synchronized
the_forecast_factory.grid: 200 km squares. 3,200 columns on the globe (actually ~12,800, he undercounted by 4×). 2,000 active columns (tropics predictable).
the_forecast_factory.math: 32 humans per active column pair × 2,000 columns = 64,000 computers to 'race the weather'
the_forecast_factory.final_line: 'Outside are playing fields, houses, mountains and lakes, for it was thought that those who compute the weather should breathe of it freely.'

our_analog.forecast_factory: our cron ring IS the forecast factory. 17 cron jobs = 17 workers, each computing a different grid cell of the membrane's state.
our_analog.64000_computers: 154,511 files in the repo. each file is a 'computer' holding one piece of the state. the cron jobs read them all.
our_analog.the_conductor: the heartbeat cron (*/3) = the conductor with colored signal lights. it synchronizes all other processes.
our_analog.grid_cells: 59 rules in the selection table = 59 grid cells of the immune atmosphere. each rule = one Richardson computer.
our_analog.racing_the_weather: */7 cron = attempting to 'race the weather' of membrane traffic. can we compute the immune state faster than traffic changes?
our_analog.breathe_freely: 'those who compute the weather should breathe of it freely' — the news desk publishes everything. the workers (cron jobs) breathe the same air (data) they compute.

richardson_1922.ref: Richardson, L.F. (1922). 'Weather Prediction by Numerical Process.' Cambridge University Press.

tiros_1960.what: TIROS-1 — first successful weather satellite. 'Television InfraRed Observational Satellite.'
tiros_1960.the_moment: the first time humans SAW weather from above. not predicted. SEEN. the storm was already there — we just couldn't see it until we had altitude.

our_analog.tiros: the thymus news desk IS our TIROS. it gives us ALTITUDE — we see the membrane's weather from above, not from inside the storm.
our_analog.orbit: the */7 cron cycle = the 99-minute orbit. each pass captures a new image of the membrane's state.
our_analog.78_days: TIROS-1 lasted 78 days. our thymus will last as long as the cron runs. it IS the satellite.
our_analog.thousands_of_images: each immune-state-live.json is one satellite image. each RSS item is one broadcast from orbit. continuous observation.

tiros_1960.first_image: Frame 1, Camera 2, Orbit M001 — received April 1, 1960. cloud cover over Gulf of Maine and Nova Scotia. the famous 'first picture' is actually Frame 8 from April 2. the REAL first image is less pretty but more true.
tiros_1960.our_first_image: immune-20261025-2011 — the first membrane report. 500 requests, SEPTIC (73.6% threat from test traffic). not pretty. but TRUE.

eniac_1950.who: Jule Charney + Ragnar Fjørtoft + John von Neumann
eniac_1950.what: first successful numerical weather prediction using ENIAC computer
eniac_1950.note: Richardson's dream realized — 28 years later. 64,000 human computers replaced by one room-sized machine.
eniac_1950.our_analog: cursor agents = our ENIAC. a single agent can compute what Richardson needed 64,000 humans for.

radiosonde_1929.what: first balloon carrying instruments to measure atmospheric temperature, pressure, humidity aloft
radiosonde_1929.note: before radiosondes, all weather observations were from the surface. radiosondes gave us the VERTICAL profile.
radiosonde_1929.our_analog: the microscope instrument (154K files, 9 size orders) IS our radiosonde. it measures the VERTICAL profile of the codebase — surface to depth.

observation_not_prediction.key: weather forecasting is NOT prediction. it is observation + physics + computation.

stages.our_analog: selection table (59 PDEs of immune classification)
first immune cycle: 500 cells classified, SEPTIC
thymus news desk (view FROM the sky)

observation_not_prediction.the_point: each step was seeing FURTHER, not guessing better. the thymus doesn't predict attacks. it SEES them. the storm is already there — we just need the altitude to observe it.

what_we_broadcast: the weather (immune vitals — health, threat pressure, antibody temperature)
the traffic (request classification — who's on the roads)
the flows (route distribution — where traffic goes after classification)
the whale-fall (death and renewal — what died, what it fed)
the fronts (self/non-self boundary shifts — where the weather is changing)
where_we_broadcast: RSS feed.xml (the news ticker — any RSS reader sees the weather)
news-latest.json (the live bulletin — HUD/connect displays it)
ntfy neutrino (the emergency broadcast — push to all subscribers)
immune-state-live.json (the raw data — for computation, not humans)
backscatter_broadcast.frequency: every 7 minutes. 205 forecasts per day. continuous radar.
backscatter_broadcast.klein: the broadcast IS the observation. the RSS feed IS the satellite image. inside the Klein surface = outside the Klein surface. the weather we see IS the weather we publish.

connections: space-weather-forecast.json (actual space weather — solar, not membrane)
